The tensor difference is nonzero by the stated linear-functional argument and nilpotent by Frobenius. Its nonzero image in a suitable localization contradicts the cited theorem that regular local rings are domains.

The section is locally constant on the two open intervals, while every global locally constant integer-valued function on connected ℝ is constant. The cited interfaces support each step, and the restriction map is not surjective.

Step 6.1 does not follow: a DVR witness cannot show that the general uniqueness criterion must quantify over all valuation rings. The example also confirms, rather than refutes, the claim that this DVR detects nonuniqueness for D.

The doubled closed point of this nondiscrete rank-one valuation ring is quasi-separated and nonseparated. A DVR cannot map its closed point to either copy while mapping its generic point to the shared generic point, so DVR lifts are unique.
